title: Committee defers reserve contribution to budget day
subtitle: Rideshare revenue, police budget share, transit cuts, bulky-item pickup, landfill cells and staff follow-up requests.
overview: The Strategic Planning and Budget Committee spent its second 2026 budget meeting hearing staff updates and questioning staff, rather than setting the budget. Staff proposed adding $335,000 in expected rideshare fee revenue and putting $2,460,000 into the Tax Stabilization Reserve, the Region's contingency fund, so residents' communicated tax increase would not change. The committee referred that motion to the December 16 budget day {{vote:m2}}, so it can be weighed alongside other councillor motions.

The committee received three reports for information: property assessment growth, the community engagement summary, and staff responses to councillor questions. It also asked staff to report back on many items, including capital reserve and project funding breakdowns, vehicle replacement standards, transit route and terminal options, seniors' transit costs, facility and professional fee increases, provincial and federal funding, and Cambridge area-rating costs.

Residents should expect the reserve contribution, transit service reductions, bulky-item pickup and other proposed savings to be debated on December 16. Councillor motions are due December 10, and a second day is set aside if needed. The committee also held a public input session that evening.

decisions.detail: The committee deferred the staff-supported motion to add $335,000 in rideshare fee revenue and contribute $2,460,000 to the Tax Stabilization Reserve to the December 16, 2025 budget meeting {{vote:m2}}.

debate: Several councillors backed topping up the Tax Stabilization Reserve, citing a projected 2025 deficit, a low balance against its $15 million policy target, and credit-rating concerns. One councillor worried even the larger balance might not cover a major shock. Another preferred using surpluses and asked whether rideshare revenue should stay with related programs.

Councillors discussed how the police budget affects the regional tax increase. Staff confirmed it is separate but part of one total tax bill, and said they will show the split on December 16. Police board members said police have been unfairly singled out. Others said asking questions is part of due diligence, not an attack.

Process was contested. Some argued the reserve motion should wait for budget day so it could be considered with other motions, as staff had said at the start. Others wanted to amend it now with looser wording on funding sources. A councillor also noted that raising the rideshare fee could change what goes to the reserve.

Councillors pressed staff on savings. Staff said cutting bulky-item pickup below monthly would save little, because fleet and staffing costs would stay similar, and a delegate-style concern was raised that reopening transfer stations might follow. Others questioned $40 million-plus in new landfill cells, but staff said capacity is about 18 to 20 years and the next cell is needed soon.

On transit, councillors asked about reduced routes, delaying a Kitchener terminal, and extra fare inspectors. Staff said enforcement is education-first and offered costings for changes. Some also pointed to Cambridge area-rating costs and veterans' passes.
